english: It's possible for ones sense powers to be skewed by force of the effects of a cataract; so that some people with cataracts may mistakenly see a strand of hair that's not actually there; or one moon that appears as two; or a spot of color like the pattern on a peacock's feathers; a random fly; or something of the like. When we say “mistakenly” here, what we mean is that—even though none of these things is actually there—our condition makes us hold to or see them as existing.
